_doc: High Plains Raceway through Lake Murray v4's engine (ledger 0078: the old quality bar, ported to check that nothing gets worse). The line, widths and 3DEP are tracks/high-plains's (installed 0.72.1), read by tools/lm_engine_intake.py; the profile is the measured one with the elevation stage's grade cap undone; the camber is the G10 lidar survey (source/lidar/camber-survey/crossfall.json, branch claude/lidar-camber-survey); the edge is the circuit's (no curb, no sidewalk). Every other key is the live track's, copied; the live config is untouched.

source._smooth_window_doc: 2026-10-29 (ledger 0060): osm_fixes.json is a list of 79 OSM nodes (18 m apart on the corners, up to 585 m on the straights), not a 1 Hz GPS drive; from_track's 5-fix moving average cut its corners by up to 26.8 m and parted the closed ring's ends by 466 m (bridged with a chord): the deck floated over ground the track is not on and the engine minted four bridges. 0 = no smoothing.
source._note: RE-SOURCED 2026-07-25 from the REAL High Plains Raceway at 93301 E US Hwy 36, Deer Trail CO (39.7353,-103.8980). Replaces fabricated compressed lat/lon traced off the old unified map (which placed it at 39.67,-104.77, ~70 km away). Geometry is the closed cycle of OSM highway=raceway ways: Short North, Bikers Berm, Niagara, Dannys Lesson, High Plains Drifter, Prarie Corkscrew, Full West + one unnamed link = 3220 m (2.00 mi). The north section (To Hell On A Bobsled / Ladder To Heaven) is EXCLUDED: its south end is unmapped in OSM, leaving a 110 m gap that would have to be invented to close the full 2.55-mile course (LAWS L1 — never invent geometry). Add it by tracing that 110 m off a georeferenced aerial, then re-chain. Pit Lane excluded (not the racing line). Winding CW to match the other CO circuits. Elevation from USGS 3DEP at the real site.
source._width_note: default_width_m 12.0 is INHERITED FROM THE FABRICATED CONFIG and unverified against the real circuit.

route._start_at_doc: 2026-10-29 (ledger 0060): the REAL S/F, mid front straight between the Prairie Corkscrew exit and T1 (~39.7350, -103.8946), as _orientation_doc gave it; until now this held the pre-July displaced frame's point (39.67456, -104.77141), 77 km from the re-sourced site, so the chain's 'rotated by 251 points to the real start line' picked an arbitrary ring point. The projection snaps to the nearest ring vertex.
route._orientation_doc: Research 2026-07-20: High Plains Raceway runs CLOCKWISE (PCA turn guide + LapMeta, 15 turns, 2.56 mi). Our ring is already CW. REAL S/F: mid front straight (~370 m, WSW->ENE ~102 deg, between the Prairie Corkscrew exit and T1) at real-world ~39.7350,-103.8946 — but THIS trace lives in a displaced frame (~77 km off; re-source pending per CLAUDE.md), so start_at is the matching straight IN THE TRACE'S OWN FRAME: the 207 m straight bearing 115.7 deg, midpoint 39.67456,-104.77141. Re-derive when re-sourced. Pit lane: real hot pits on the NORTH side of the front straight (driver's left), ~690 m incl. entry/exit; entry before S/F at the corkscrew exit, exit wraps outside T1-T2 and merges at T2 exit.

edge._doc: the circuit edge (ledger 0078): no curb, no sidewalk (neither track has one). The asphalt edge is held at road height for 0.30 m and the run-off ground meets it 0.15 m lower over 1.0 m [invented: the flush meet the drive gate reads as no drop]; the ground beyond is the assembler's conform to the road (20 m + 16 m blend), then the 3DEP surface: the real run-off level. Racing kerbs and paved run-off are NOT built: no measured kerb line or run-off outline is committed for either track (owed: read off the NAIP / lidar).

route._kerbs_doc: the racing kerbs traced off the aerial (tracks/high-plains/source/edges/kerbs.json: imagery, method, the eye check); built by tools/author_kerbs_blend.py outside the lane edge, the config's kerb profile
